article.title: Chapter Notes: October 2026
article.author: Pinellas DSA
article.content: We recruited the 400th member of Pinellas DSA this month — and we’re still growing! BOO, comrade! An extra-spooky Halloween edition of the Pinellas DSA newsletter is here! We hit another exciting milestone in September — our chapter is now officially more than 400 members strong! That’s 400 friends and neighbors who’ve made the choice to stand up and say “I believe that a better world is possible.” And, as long as we keep doing the day-to-day work of building our organization and growing the international movement for socialism, we will transform possible into inevitable . Read on to learn more about what our chapter was up to over the last month, and what we have coming up next! September Highlights PDSA comrades at the September Interest Meeting & New Member Orientation. September was a month of steady progress for our ongoing campaigns. Perhaps the biggest development came early in the month when DSA comrades behind the Dump Duke campaign held a press conference in Williams Park to announce the launch of a petition campaign to place an amendment for public power on the 2028 ballot. Meanwhile, organizers behind the No on 3 initiative wasted no time, launching a series of door-to-door canvasses, lit drops, and more to get the word out about the threat Amendment 3 poses to our communities. We also established a social media presence for our DeFlock St. Pete campaign, which has already seen a major win with a new business item in front of the St. Pete City Council, introduced by Councilmember and DSA comrade Richie Floyd, to allow for the discussion of the city’s Flock contract. We also published the first in a fantastic new series of videos from our International Solidarity Working Group, with the aim of educating the masses on the legacy of US imperialism in the Caribbean. Check it out on the official Pinellas DSA YouTube channel (and subscribe while you’re at it)! Lastly, we want to also spotlight the Pinellas DSA blog , which is where you can find updates and official statements published on behalf of the chapter. We’re also accepting submissions for the blog from any active member in good standing; email us at dsa.pinellas@gmail.com if you’d like to pitch your article! CAMPAIGN UPDATE: Dump Duke On September 2, Pinellas DSA members held a press conference to announce the launch of a petition campaign to place a charter amendment on the 2028 ballot. If successful, the initiative would give St. Pete voters the opportunity to decide whether the city should establish a publicly owned electric utility. The event, which was held in Williams Park — directly across the street from Duke Energy headquarters — was also the official launch of Public Power St. Pete, a coalition aimed at advancing the #DumpDuke mission. Besides Pinellas DSA, other coalition members include the CLEO Institute, Sierra Club Suncoast Group, Florida Youth Action Fund, People Power for Florida, and Florida Rising. At the heart of this campaign is a simple goal: making electricity more affordable, reliable, and locally controlled for St. Pete residents. It won’t be easy, though: organizers will need to collect 16,200 petitions with verified signatures from St. Pete voters, with the aim to secure over 20,000 signatures. Learn more about the petition drive here CAMPAIGN UPDATE: DeFlock St. Pete As mentioned above, Councilmember Richie Floyd introducing a business item during a meeting of the St. Pete City Council at the end of August to allow for the discussion of the city’s Flock contract. Specifically, how we can eliminate it . You might reasonably assume that this initiative would see pushback from at least a few of the council’s more conservative members. However, St. Pete City Council voted unanimously to pass this item, and advance the discussion to the city’s Public Services & Infrastructure Committee. Richie sits on the committee, as do Councilmembers Hanewicz, Harting, and Gerdes. Organizers with the DeFlock St. Pete campaign are asking anyone who is “passionate about preventing our little slice of Florida from becoming part of the surveillance state” to reach out to the three committee members in question, thank them for backing Richie’s business item, and let them know that you want to #DeFlockStPete! You can reach the officials in question using the contact information provided below: Copley Gerdes: copley.gerdes@stpete.org | (727) 551–3528 Mike Harting: mike.harting@stpete.org | (727) 551–3305 Lisset Hanewicz: lisset.hanewicz@stpete.org | (727) 893–7412 CAMPAIGN UPDATE: No on 3 PDSA comrades out knocking doors to get out the vote against Amendment 3. Organizers behind the No on 3 campaign hit the ground running last month, launching into a series of door-to-door canvasses, lit drops, and “public service stakeouts” to rally Pinellas residents to defeat Amendment 3 on the November ballot. If Amendment 3 passes, Pinellas County residents will suffer from millions of dollars in public funding cuts each year, impacting EMS, fire and rescue, flood mitigation, infrastructure repair, libraries, parks, public transit, and more. This campaign was spun up on short notice, withe less than three months to get the word out. But, organizers have done a phenomenal job so far!
